Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking this — Medivalue is wrapping up the SIG/SOC2 evidentiary packet and we need a concise collection of access control artifacts from Redwood to close a few controls. Specifically we need:

- SAML assertion samples (redacted) for a handful of authentication flows (SSO -> app)
- A SCIM delta export that shows user provisioning/deprovisioning events for the last 90 days (CSV or similar)
- RBAC / role ownership matrix showing who owns high-priv roles and what those roles map to
- A short narrative (1-2 pages) explaining least-privilege enforcement for service accounts and delegated roles

One additional ask: our security reviewer has a scenario question — in the event of a suspected credential compromise (service account keys or long-lived tokens), what is your detection and containment playbook and how quickly can you isolate sessions or revoke affected keys? If you can include any SLAs or recent tabletop results that demonstrate time-to-contain, that will help us a lot.

Can you provide the artifacts (or a secure drive link) within 3 business days? If anything requires redaction or we should accept sampled artifacts instead of full exports, let us know.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

Sean / team — I can take the SCIM export and saml samples. Quick notes on scope and redaction: 

1) SCIM delta: we'll produce a 90-day delta CSV sampled at a 1-in-5 rate (to protect PII) and include an index that maps sampled rows to event types. Fields: timestamp, actor_principal, event_type (create/update/delete), target_type (user/group), target_id (redacted), attributes_changed. File: scim-delta-sample-202606.csv (attached).

2) SAML assertions: we will include three redacted assertion examples (interactive user SSO, SAML-for-service-account, and an IdP-initiated flow). All nameIDs and user identifiers will be hashed. File: saml-assertion-samples-redacted.txt (attached).

3) RBAC matrix: Laura will assemble a role->permission->owner matrix. Suggested file: rbac-ownership-matrix.xlsx. Please confirm if Medivalue prefers raw role IDs or human-readable role names; legal tends to prefer redacted IDs for third-party disclosure.

4) Least-priv narrative: Vanessa will draft a one-page PDF describing enforcement controls (role reviews, just-in-time admin, ephemeral tokens, service account rotation cadence). File: least-privilege-justification.pdf (to be attached).

Breach-scenario answer (short):
- Detection: anomalous token usage triggers telemetry rules (rate-of-use, geo anomalies, unusual API calls). Alerts route to SOC and our automated playbook.
- Containment: tokens and keys are revokable via the central credential service; we can revoke a token immediately and expire any active sessions within the affected tenant. For service accounts we enforce key rotation by policy (90 days default) and maintain a revocation endpoint.
- Measured SLA: in the last tabletop we simulated a compromised service token and achieved containment within ~23 minutes from detection to token revocation (SOC led exercise, May 2026). We'll include the exercise summary in the bundle.

I'm attaching the two artifacts we have ready now. Laura/Vanessa — please add your files to the drive link and ping me when done so I can assemble final zip.

Irene Choi

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a secure bundle with redacted samples and our narrative addressing the breach scenario. Contents (brief):

- access-evidence-bundle-20260730.zip (contains)
  - saml-assertion-samples-redacted.txt (3 samples, hashed identifiers)
  - scim-delta-sample-202606.csv (1-in-5 sampled delta, index included)
  - rbac-ownership-matrix.xlsx (role -> permission -> owner view; PII minimized)
  - least-privilege-justification.pdf (1 page)
  - tabletop-summary-may2026.pdf (redacted exercise results)

Breach-scenario summary (short):
- Detection: automated telemetry flags anomalous token patterns (rate, geo, resource anomalies).
- Containment: central credential service supports immediate token/key revocation. We isolate sessions by invalidating session cookies and pushing session-expire signals to runtime nodes; tenant-scoped keys are revoked centrally.
- Measured result: May 2026 tabletop — mean time from detection to revoke = ~23 minutes; full recovery (root cause and remediation checklist) averaged 4 hours in that exercise.

If you prefer the full, un-sampled SCIM export for a dedicated compliance channel (with an NDA/secure transfer), we can arrange that off-band. Otherwise this bundle should meet SIG/SOC2 control evidence needs.
